summary: This note documents the CURRENT_ROLE_TYPE() function, which reports whether the active role in the session is an account role or a database role. It returns ROLE for an account role and DATABASE_ROLE for a database role. The page lists its syntax, states it takes no arguments and has no usage notes, and gives a SELECT example that returns ROLE.
one_line: Reference for the CURRENT_ROLE_TYPE() session function, which returns ROLE or DATABASE_ROLE for the session's active role.
key_facts: CURRENT_ROLE_TYPE returns either ROLE or DATABASE_ROLE.
It returns ROLE when the current active role in the session is an account role.
It returns DATABASE_ROLE when the current active role in the session is a database role.
The page lists no usage notes for the function.
The example query SELECT CURRENT_ROLE_TYPE(); returns ROLE.
The function belongs to the Session Object category, under the Session section of the reference.
